title: The Problem With Selling Digital Products from Africa and How to Solve It at the Base Layer
author: COREMERCH
excerpt: Selling digital products from Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, Bangladesh, or Zimbabwe is fully operational with sovereign commerce infrastructure that has no geographic restrictions.

content.text: Creators in Africa, particularly in Nigeria, Ghana, and Kenya, face significant barriers when selling digital products online due to restrictions from platforms like Stripe and PayPal, limiting their access to international buyers. This problem is not unique to Africa, as creators in Pakistan, Bangladesh, and other regions also struggle with similar issues. The lack of suitable payment infrastructure hinders the growth of digital commerce in these areas.
The Real Reason This Problem Exists

The primary reason for this issue is the absence of reliable, accessible payment processing systems that cater to the needs of digital creators in these regions. Traditional payment gateways often have stringent requirements, high fees, or are simply not available, leaving creators without a viable means to receive payments from international customers. This gap in infrastructure severely limits the potential for digital commerce in affected countries.
Why the Obvious Fixes Do Not Work

Workarounds such as using third-party payment processors or makeshift solutions may seem appealing but often introduce new challenges, including higher transaction fees, increased complexity, and reduced reliability. These fixes do not address the underlying issue of infrastructure deficiency and may even lead to further complications, such as payment disputes or account suspensions. A more robust and permanent solution is necessary to support the growth of digital commerce in these regions.
The Infrastructure That Solves It at the Base Layer

The implementation of blockchain-based payment systems, such as those utilizing cryptocurrencies, offers a promising solution. By leveraging platforms like NOWPayments, which supports over 300 cryptocurrencies and charges a minimal fee of 0.5%, creators can receive payments directly without relying on intermediaries.
